body:
## Why

#548 merged real SNAP QC reports at 01:54 UTC on 2026-09-23. Starting four hours later, the 6-hourly affected rerun overwrote five of them with re-emissions:

| State | Commit |
| --- | --- |
| NY | db02c1f04 |
| MD | 25684f0fb |
| AZ | f4a815f89 |
| CA | df7678e90 |
| GA | 804c42cc8 |

Every later sweep repeated the overwrite. Each commit sets `provenance.reemitted_report: true` and `run_kind: affected-rerun`, and drops `rulespecs`. Only the provenance changed; the numbers are identical. rulespec-us main had not moved from f43dec52 when this started.

The cause, read from the code:

- **The map listed repos the replay never reads.** `comparisons/affected_map.json` mapped each snap-qc suite to `rulespec-us` and to `rulespec-us-<st>`. Every `rulespec-us-<st>` repo was archived on 2026-06-27 ("ARCHIVED: absorbed into rulespec-us/us-<st>").
  - `build_overlay` copies both `us/` and `us-<st>/` out of one rulespec-us checkout.
  - The engine is pointed at that overlay alone.
  - So a live report can only ever record the rulespec-us SHA, and `select_affected_suites.py` picked every snap-qc suite on every sweep ("rulespec-us-<st>: report ran against unknown SHA").
- **The legs could only re-emit.** They clone rulespec-us main but never build the engine or download the QC file. `run_comparison.py` therefore re-emitted, and `commit_refreshed_report.sh` committed the result. Once a re-emission was committed, the report had no provenance at all, so the suite kept being re-selected even when rulespec-us didn't move.
- **Why CO survived.** Its case chunks use a versioned index, which already sent it down the existing preserve-on-skip path. The other six suites have unversioned indexes.
- **The herd.** In run 35786994281, the GA leg logged 22 push rejections and was cancelled at 90 minutes; MD was cancelled at the same point.

Reproduction: `select_affected_suites.py --heads-json <file> --format json`, where the heads file holds rulespec-us plus the seven `rulespec-us-<st>` HEADs from `gh api repos/<repo>/commits/HEAD`.

| | CO and GA (real at the time) | NY, CA, AZ, MD, TX (already re-emitted) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **origin/main map** | selected and dispatched: `rulespec-us-<st>: report ran against unknown SHA` | selected and dispatched: `report has no provenance` |
| **this PR** | fresh against the SHA they ran on, so not selected | restored, so fresh; when rulespec-us moves they are listed for the manual lane (`name: null`) and never dispatched |

## What

1. **Affected map.** `generate_affected_map.py` maps a `snap-qc-compare` suite to exactly the rulespec root its overlay is built from: rulespec-us, or the basename of an explicit `rulespec_root`. For this runner type, concept prefixes and the jurisdiction no longer add repos. Only the seven snap-qc entries change. The report already records the SHA of the repo the state layer comes from (rulespec-us), so "fix the map" and "record that SHA" are the same change.
2. **Routing.** The seven `comparisons/*-snap-qc.yaml` files declare `ci: manual`, each with the house-style comment saying why and what unblocks it.
   - The map gives them `name: null`. The selector lists stale ones for the manual lane and never dispatches them.
   - `comparisons.yml` skips them. Its snap-qc legs only ever re-emitted and uploaded artifacts, and it commits no reports.
   - `only: <st>-snap-qc` now says the suite is `ci: manual` instead of "unknown comparison".
3. **Guard: a marked re-emission never replaces a report from a real run.** This applies to every lane.
   - `run_comparison.py _write_dashboard_report` now leaves any committed real report byte-for-byte unchanged on a skip. It extends the existing rule, which covered only versioned reports. An unstamped legacy report counts as real.
   - `_preserved_versioned_source_is_output` is widened the same way, so a same-day skip cannot overwrite the `reports/` file a preserved copy points at.
   - The shared predicate is `axiom_oracles.provenance.is_real_run_report`.
   - `scripts/guard_reemitted_reports.py` runs in `commit_refreshed_report.sh`'s push loop on every attempt, after the reset to the tip. It puts back the tip's bytes for any top-level dashboard report whose working copy is a marked re-emission while the tip's copy is real. That makes it safe for a real report that lands while a leg is running.
   - This matters because bot pushes (GITHUB_TOKEN) never run `ci.yml`.
   - A re-emission over a re-emission, and a first report, still publish as before.
4. **Data.** NY, CA, AZ, GA and MD are restored to #548's bytes (ff551a95b). TX is restored to a1a22f1fe (#279), its only real run: July 2026, rulespec-us 53ae9199, on the May QC posting's weights. Every later TX version was a re-emission, and the one on main claimed the August pin over those July numbers. Regenerated: `freshness.json`, `overview.json`, `conformance/exercise-census.json`, and the census sha256 in the three certificates that pin it. DE artifacts are untouched.
5. **Docs.** `comparisons/README.md`, `README.md`, the playbook, the YAML descriptions, the workflow comments and the docstrings now match.
   - The weekly matrix is described as a CI signal. It only uploads reports and never commits them, so "backstop" was wrong.
   - A stale docstring said fy-2024-cola lived only on a rulespec-us branch. It has been on main since rulespec-us#760.

## What `comparisons.yml` and the freshness gate do now

- **`comparisons.yml`:** the weekly matrix drops the seven snap-qc legs, going from 75 to 68.
- **`check_vacuous_gate.py`:** `freshness.json` records `affected_repos: [rulespec-us]` for the seven, plus the restored real provenance.
  - Staleness past 14 days is a render-time dashboard alarm, not a CI failure.
  - rulespec-us main is now dcb2e47e, five commits past f43dec52. The six reports will age into that alarm unless a supervised run refreshes them or the stacked live lane lands. TX already shows July.

## Verification

- **CI.** Run 35947454078 passed on this change's first build (59f40604d) on ubuntu x86_64. That covers every gate, including `certify.py --check` for the DE certificates, the full suite, and `gettsim-live`. This head adds the review fixes and a rebuild on the current main tip.
- **New tests.** They fail on origin/main and pass here:
  - `tests/test_affected_map.py`:
    - snap-qc maps only the replayed root;
    - every snap-qc suite is `ci: manual` / `name: null`;
    - the map's repos equal what `_build_run_provenance` records for a real run;
    - every committed snap-qc report is a real run with a rulespec-us SHA, which fails if main's re-emitted CA/GA/MD/TX copies come back in a rebase;
    - the selector never dispatches snap-qc and leaves fresh ones alone.
  - `tests/test_run_comparison.py`:
    - a real unversioned report survives a skip;
    - a re-emission, or a first copy, still publishes;
    - a real run still replaces a real report;
    - end to end through `main()` for `ny-snap-qc`, the 2026-09-23 path;
    - the widened source-pointer guard.
  - `tests/test_guard_reemitted_reports.py`, 7 cases:
    - the tip's revision is what counts;
    - unreadable reports are ignored;
    - the checkout uses a literal pathspec.
  - `tests/test_commit_refreshed_report.py`:
    - the guard's position in the push loop;
    - a hermetic end-to-end run that keeps the tip's real NY report and whose push never touches it.
  - `tests/test_provenance.py` covers the predicate.
- **Gates run locally on this head:** `generate_affected_map`, `check_vacuous_gate`, `generate_dashboard_overview`, `exercise_census`, `conformance_scoreboard`, `conformance_burndown`, `apply_dispositions`, `generate_chunk_indexes`, `unexplained_ratchet`, `conformance_ratchet` and `closure_universe` all pass with `--check`, as does `certify.py --check` for the three certificates this PR touches.
  - On an aarch64 Mac the DE replay cannot run the pinned x86_64 engine. Eight DE, dk and commit-script tests fail locally for that reason, identically on unmodified main.
- **Independent review.** Five parallel lenses (guard, routing, data integrity, a claims audit, completeness), each medium-or-higher finding checked by a skeptic. Fixes applied:
  - GA was missing from the overwrite count.
  - The docs claimed the CI legs lack the rulespec-us checkout; they lack the engine and the QC file.
  - The marker-drop condition could have invited a regression once #549 lands.
  - "Weekly backstop" wording.
  - The guard's pathspec and UTF-8 handling.
  - A stronger end-to-end assertion.
  - The data review verified all 174 certificate hash pins: 170 match, 4 external, 0 mismatch.

## Scope and interplay

- **Live affected-rerun legs** (the optional third item) are in draft #553, stacked on #549 and this PR. The affected rerun calls #549's replay lane for stale SNAP QC suites and commits only reports the lane proved live and exact. A GitHub trial ran all six replays exactly against rulespec-us `dcb2e47e` and exercised the commit path in simulate mode without pushing.
- **#549** merges with this cleanly in either order, so git will not flag that its README sentence, the playbook §10 opening, the `snap-qc-replay.yml` header and the `snap_qc_replay.py` docstring still say the weekly matrix and the affected rerun dispatch snap-qc and re-emit. #553 (stacked on #549 and this PR) rewrites those passages; if #549 lands without it, they need that edit.
- **UK PolicyEngine case-grid runners** (uk-vat, CTR, CGT, and others) copy the committed report on fallback without marking it, so this guard cannot see them. #549 adds the marker.
- **Not addressed:** the re-emit-over-re-emit churn from about 35 EUROMOD/UKMOD and us-tariff suites, where committed reports that are already re-emissions are re-committed with a new timestamp every sweep. Those lanes' earlier real runs (for example be-marital-quotient on 2026-08-21, and us-tariff 034741c63) were overwritten the same way. Both are left for a separate change.

## Merge procedure

A leg that is inside its push loop when this merges keeps running the old commit script: bash has already parsed the loop. It resets to the new main, restores the re-emission it produced, and can push it.

1. Disable the rerun, or check that nothing is running or queued:

   ```
   gh workflow disable affected-rerun.yml
   gh run list --workflow affected-rerun.yml --status in_progress
   gh run list --workflow affected-rerun.yml --status queued
   ```

2. If main moved, rebase and regenerate. Bot commits rewrite `freshness.json`, `overview.json`, the exercise census, and the three census-pinning certificates. Keep this PR's six snap-qc reports, take main's derived files, then rerun `generate_affected_map`, `check_vacuous_gate`, `generate_dashboard_overview` and `exercise_census`, and re-pin the census sha in the three certificates. `test_committed_snap_qc_reports_are_real_runs` fails if a resolution drops a restored report.
3. Merge, then `gh workflow enable affected-rerun.yml`.
4. After the next sweep, check that `git rev-parse origin/main:dashboard/public/data/axiom-snapqc-<st>-snap.json` still equals this PR's blobs for all six states.

title: Stop the affected rerun from overwriting real SNAP QC reports
